messages:
sara (monitoring): Alert: hosted-infer tenant=acme-app reporting spike of 503s from upstream inference workers starting ~2026-03-17T10:12Z. QPS 180->800, 503 rate ~30/min. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-infer?orgId=1&panelId=503s :rotating_light:

jon (cs-ops): Customer ACME reporting timeouts, opened support ticket #12345. CS asks for ETA and mitigation. They say some requests 30s+ until gateway returns 503.

mike (eng-runtime): I'm seeing repeated worker exits on the same host pool. Logs show SIGSEGV in attention kernel during KV prefetch, then container restart by watchdog. Collecting core and nvml output now.

alisha (eng-sre): Can we route traffic away from that pool? Suggest immediate: add a routing rule to avoid pool=eu-west-2-hotprefetch and reduce max_batch_size to 1 for acme-app to reduce mem pressure.

ingrid (prodops): On it — flipping routing to fallback pool (cpu-fallback) for acme-app now, and starting rolling restart of the affected node group (nicely throttled). deploy-bot: started restart job for nodegroup-ng-7.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart job started for nodegroup-ng-7 (5 instances). progress: 0/5

mike (eng-runtime): Pasted a quick tail of the kernel output: ```
[2026-03-17T10:13:02Z] infer-runner[2345]: prefretch_kv: allocating kv_size=2.4G
[2026-03-17T10:13:03Z] infer-runner[2345]: nvml: out-of-memory on device 0, free=120MB, req=2.4GB
[2026-03-17T10:13:03Z] infer-runner[2345]: *** SIGSEGV in attn_kernel.cu:0x7f9a12
```
Looks like a memory balloon during prefetch triggers OOM then segfault in custom attn kernel. Not a simple graceful OOM.

alisha (eng-sre): Any GPU driver/ECC messages? NVML verbose?

mike (eng-runtime): nvml output included ECC=corrected, but driver logs show: `kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU fell off the bus` and `nvidia: GPU reset` around same time. Also noticed CUDA driver 515.x was rolled on those hosts yesterday during a maintenance window.

jon (cs-ops): Customer wants mitigation now. They've been routed to cpu-fallback but performance plummets. Offering ACME a credit and realtime updates.

ingrid (prodops): Restart roll completed on nodegroup-ng-7, deploy-bot: 5/5. After restart, we still see occasional 503s but lower rate. I'm keeping routing to cpu-fallback for acme-app until further notice.

mike (eng-runtime): I pulled one core dump and ran addr2line. Stack points to quantized attention path + kv-prefetch hot path. Repro appears when context_length > 200k tokens (rare), combined with dynbatch expansion. Reproduced locally by replaying their request (thanks to CS provided request id). Attaching minimal repro steps:
1) start runner with `--kv-prefetch=true --quantize=int8 --batch-map=dynamic`
2) send request with context ~250k tokens (we used a trimmed dump)
3) observe `nvml error: out of memory` then segfault in `attn_cuda_kernel.cu`

Snippet: ```
$ ./runner --kv-prefetch --quantize=int8
curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"<big context...>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
# kernel crash -> core
```

alisha (eng-sre): Immediate actions agreed: (A) pin driver back to 510.x on impacted pool, (B) force route acme-app to safer pools (done), (C) roll kernel patch that introduced aggressive prefetch heuristic. Long term: add cgroup clamp for kv-prefetch and a graceful OOM path for attention kernel.

mike (eng-runtime): Filed RC INF-2026-45 for rollout & revert: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2026-45. Root cause hypothesis: regressed attention kernel interaction with CUDA 515 driver under large KV prefetch leading to NVML OOM + segfault.

jon (cs-ops): Noted customer comms and credit offer. Keeping ACME on cpu-fallback for now; will update #12345 and escalate SLA if needed.

ingrid (prodops): Post-incident: I've pinned drivers on nodegroup-ng-7 back to 510.3 and disabled aggressive prefetch on the pool. Watching metrics — 503s dropped to baseline.

mike (eng-runtime): Follow-up checklist: collect all core dumps, correlate with driver versions, add an integration test for large-context prefetch, add runtime guard to avoid prefetch if free_gpu_mem < 1.5GB. I'll own the postmortem and timeline.

jon (cs-ops): Thanks — CS will send a short status update to ACME and include timeline for permanent fix. :thumbsup:

ingrid (prodops): Monitoring link for followups: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-infer?orgId=1&view=acme-app-503s

mike (eng-runtime): Final note: if anyone has reproduced this locally with CUDA 515 let me know. I pushed a debug build with extra NVML checks to the staging pool.

alisha (eng-sre): Closing on-call handoff in 30m. We'll track INF-2026-45 and postmortem in infra-ops.

sara (monitoring): Alert cleared at 2026-03-17T10:34Z; rate returned to baseline after driver pin + routing.
